commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
Enable freestanding builds for IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC

Avoid assuming POSIX facilities are available on Generic platforms,
allowing the runtime to build for freestanding/bare-metal targets.

This disables POSIX-dependent functionality such as sockets and singal
handling by default, avoids selecting a POSIX async proactor, and
provides the small platform fallbacks needed by the Generic runtime
build.

This commit also fixes build-system issues encountered while bringing up the
Generic RISCV configuration.

Assisted-by: Claude code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

Avoid assuming POSIX facilities are available on Generic platforms,
allowing the runtime to build for freestanding/bare-metal targets.

This disables POSIX-dependent functionality such as sockets and singal
handling by default, avoids selecting a POSIX async proactor, and
provides the small platform fallbacks needed by the Generic runtime
build.

This commit also fixes build-system issues encountered while bringing up the
Generic RISCV configuration.

Assisted-by: Claude code
Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_clang_tsan

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no

commit_message:
[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

the platform call, and each broke differently once a span exceeded what
that call can express:

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

None of the three file backends bounded the span length they handed to
the platform call, and each broke differently once a span exceeded what
that call can express:

  - io_uring narrowed to the 32-bit sqe->len and IOCP to a DWORD, so a
    span that is an exact multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero. The operation
    then completed successfully having moved no bytes, which the caller
    cannot distinguish from EOF.
  - posix passed the length straight to pread/pwrite, where POSIX leaves
    the result implementation-defined past SSIZE_MAX. Darwin rejects
    nbyte > INT_MAX with EINVAL; Linux quietly caps at MAX_RW_COUNT, so
    the defect only surfaced on macOS.

Clamp in all three. Short transfers are part of the file read/write
contract, so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX
rounded down to a page, which sits under Darwin's limit and matches
MAX_RW_COUNT on a 4KB-page kernel.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

the platform call, and each broke differently once a span exceeded what
that call can express:

  - io_uring narrowed to the 32-bit sqe->len and IOCP to a DWORD, so a
    span that is an exact multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero. The operation
    then completed successfully having moved no bytes, which the caller
    cannot distinguish from EOF.
  - posix passed the length straight to pread/pwrite, where POSIX leaves
    the result implementation-defined past SSIZE_MAX. Darwin rejects
    nbyte > INT_MAX with EINVAL; Linux quietly caps at MAX_RW_COUNT, so
    the defect only surfaced on macOS.

Clamp in all three. Short transfers are part of the file read/write
contract, so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX
rounded down to a page, which sits under Darwin's limit and matches
MAX_RW_COUNT on a 4KB-page kernel.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

None of the three file backends bounded the span length they handed to
the platform call, and each broke differently once a span exceeded what
that call can express:

  - io_uring narrowed to the 32-bit sqe->len and IOCP to a DWORD, so a
    span that is an exact multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero. The operation
    then completed successfully having moved no bytes, which the caller
    cannot distinguish from EOF.
  - posix passed the length straight to pread/pwrite, where POSIX leaves
    the result implementation-defined past SSIZE_MAX. Darwin rejects
    nbyte > INT_MAX with EINVAL; Linux quietly caps at MAX_RW_COUNT, so
    the defect only surfaced on macOS.

Clamp in all three. Short transfers are part of the file read/write
contract, so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX
rounded down to a page, which sits under Darwin's limit and matches
MAX_RW_COUNT on a 4KB-page kernel.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

None of the three file backends bounded the span length they handed to
the platform call, and each broke differently once a span exceeded what
that call can express:

  - io_uring narrowed to the 32-bit sqe->len and IOCP to a DWORD, so a
    span that is an exact multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero. The operation
    then completed successfully having moved no bytes, which the caller
    cannot distinguish from EOF.
  - posix passed the length straight to pread/pwrite, where POSIX leaves
    the result implementation-defined past SSIZE_MAX. Darwin rejects
    nbyte > INT_MAX with EINVAL; Linux quietly caps at MAX_RW_COUNT, so
    the defect only surfaced on macOS.

Clamp in all three. Short transfers are part of the file read/write
contract, so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX
rounded down to a page, which sits under Darwin's limit and matches
MAX_RW_COUNT on a 4KB-page kernel.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

The io_uring and IOCP backends narrowed the span length to their native
transfer count (sqe->len is 32 bits, ReadFile/WriteFile take a DWORD).
Spans over 4GB transferred the wrong amount, and a span that is an exact
multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero: the operation completed successfully
having moved no bytes, which the caller cannot distinguish from EOF.

Clamp instead. Short transfers are part of the file read/write contract,
so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX rounded
down to a page, matching the kernel's MAX_RW_COUNT.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

commit_message:
[async] Clamp file read/write lengths to the platform transfer limit

The io_uring and IOCP backends narrowed the span length to their native
transfer count (sqe->len is 32 bits, ReadFile/WriteFile take a DWORD).
Spans over 4GB transferred the wrong amount, and a span that is an exact
multiple of 4GB wrapped to zero: the operation completed successfully
having moved no bytes, which the caller cannot distinguish from EOF.

Clamp instead. Short transfers are part of the file read/write contract,
so callers resubmit for the remainder. The ceiling is INT_MAX rounded
down to a page, matching the kernel's MAX_RW_COUNT.

Adds a CTS test covering the exact-4GB case, using a sparse reservation
so the oversized span costs address space rather than committed memory.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand (#24803)

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

commit_message:
Enable freestanding builds for IREE_PLATFORM_GENERIC

Avoid assuming POSIX facilities are available on Generic platforms,
allowing the runtime to build for freestanding/bare-metal targets.

This disables POSIX-dependent functionality such as sockets and singal
handling by default, avoids selecting a POSIX async proactor, and
provides the small platform fallbacks needed by the Generic runtime
build.

This commit also fixes build-system issues encountered while bringing up the
Generic RISCV configuration.
